title: Capture Core2 WDT-off late state and reconcile project documentation

execution.environment: macOS arm64, Python 3.13, Node v22.14.0, QEMU virtual Core2

checks.name: artifact_binding
checks.detail: Current QEMU binary SHA matches the committed late-state evidence.

checks.name: late_state_repeatability
checks.detail: 45-second and 120-second WDT-off snapshots have the same CPU state and frozen Flash/SSI counters.

checks.name: flash_scan_terminal_state
checks.detail: Flash/SSI activity ends around 44 seconds; cross-core writes continue, then CPU1 remains in the same late loop.

checks.name: normal_wdt_product_path
checks.detail: The same firmware still resets at TG0 stage-1 without REPL or a non-empty application frame.

checks.name: stale_claim_guard
checks.detail: Retired startup-time and aggregate-Flash-throughput claims are rejected by current-document contracts.

checks.name: backlog_ownership
checks.detail: Backlog keeps one replayable baseline, current blockers and next steps; diagnostic IDs and run history remain in status/evidence documents.

checks.name: new_qemu_45_120_rerun
checks.detail: This consolidation did not launch another long WDT-off control.

notes: WDT disabled is a diagnostic control, not a product fix.
The late CPU1 flag/object has no matching ELF symbol.
The late-state evidence is committed, but no new 45/120-second QEMU run was launched during consolidation.
All functional results are virtual-device validation.
